taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-b-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-18, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 15.7 | 1.56 | 1.56
2 | 188.9 | 15.69 | 17.25
3 | 183.8 | 0.79 | 18.04
4 | 106.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-18, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station T-18 in survey area T consists of four interpreted layers. The resistivity profile begins with a layer of 15.7 $\Omega$m, followed by a significantly more resistive second layer of 188.9 $\Omega$m. The sequence then shows a decrease in resistivity through the third layer (183.8 $\Omega$m) and the fourth layer (106.9 $\Omega$m). Based on these values, the correct curve notation is KQ. Please note that the A-type classification currently on file is incorrect, as the layer values indicate a decrease in resistivity after the second layer rather than a continuous increase.

{"curve_type_stated": "KQ", "label_issue_flagged": true}
